paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: Training loss curves for the post-training setting.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss curves for different configurations of the SepLLM model during post-training, compared to a baseline “Vanilla before post-training” model. The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from approximately 95,000 to 125,000 iterations with linear spacing and major tick marks every 5,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.0 to 3.0 with linear scaling and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Four distinct curves are shown: a pink solid line with circular markers representing “SepLLM (n=64, larger lr),” which starts near 3.0 and steadily declines to approximately 2.25; a dark blue solid line with circular markers for “SepLLM (n=128),” beginning near 3.0 and decreasing to about 2.3; an orange solid line with circular markers for “SepLLM (n=64),” starting near 3.0 and settling around 2.35; and a red dashed horizontal line for “Vanilla before post-training,” which remains constant at approximately 2.35 across all iterations. All SepLLM variants exhibit a consistent downward trend in loss, with the “n=64, larger lr” configuration achieving the lowest final loss.
